blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Connaught Heights is the City of New Westminster's west-end mainland neighbourhood, around 22nd Street Station, London Street and Marine Way — the City name and the board sub-area name match, and the City documents Connaught Heights in its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements.

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses are effectively the whole stock here: single-detached houses under the RS (Single Detached Residential) districts of Zoning Bylaw No.

The RS-1 lot standard is the measurable lot fact: a minimum site area of 557.40 square metres (6,000 square feet) and a floor space ratio cap of 0.5; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The 22nd Street Station area is a Frequent Transit Development Area in Our City 2041, the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 7925, 2017): the City directs higher-density, transit-supportive growth there, so lots near the station carry a different planning future than the interior London Street house streets.
6680, 2001; townhouse districts RT-A and RT-B, where designated, require a minimum site area of 836.1 square metres (9,000 square feet) and minimum frontage of 20 metres.

Connaught Heights houses also sit in a documented heritage context: the neighbourhood is in Volume 3 of the City Heritage Resource Inventory (Sapperton, Victory Heights, Queensborough, Connaught Heights, West End, Kelvin and Glenbrooke).

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The elementary school shares its park with the public, with a catch: Connaught Heights Park is shared with Connaught Heights Elementary, and the City's small-sites consultation heard that the shared park is not always accessible to the community during the school day; a recommended action in the City's Comprehensive Parks Plan is to acquire more parkland in Connaught Heights.
Grimston Park is the community park at the west end of the city, the larger park serving these house streets.

The nearest City recreation facilities are east of the area: Moody Park Arena at 701 8th Avenue, with the Moody Park outdoor pool and spray park, and the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue, the city's main aquatic centre.

Electricity is a City bill, not a BC Hydro bill: New Westminster owns and operates its own electric utility under the Utility Commission Bylaw No. 8029, 2018, and the Utility Commission page lists the outage line at 604-239-6100 and billing at 604-527-4555.
The Main Branch of New Westminster Public Library is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown, east of the area — there is no library branch in Connaught Heights.

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: development and new projects

items.t: 22nd Street Station Frequent Transit Development Area, around 22nd Street Station, City of New Westminster Official Community Plan designation: higher-density, transit-supportive growth directed to the station area — STATUS: adopted plan designation in Our City 2041 (Bylaw No. 7925, 2017), read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Connaught Heights-specific cost is the suite line on the utility bill: the City's 2026 utility rates price a single-family dwelling with a secondary suite separately, at a net $4,143.46 for water, sewer and solid waste against $2,753.73 for a single-family dwelling without one — a legal suite here carries a stated annual utility premium.

22nd Street Station (Expo Line) is in the neighbourhood, and TransLink's Burnaby–New Westminster schedule lists routes 100 (Marpole), 101 (Lougheed Station), 104 (Annacis Island, via Queensborough) and 128 (Braid Station) from the station.

Route 104 is the direct bus to Queensborough: from 22nd Street Station via 7th Avenue, 20th Street and Marine Drive, across the Queensborough Bridge and Highway 91A to Howes Street and Ewen Avenue, per TransLink's timetable effective September 7, 2026.

blocks.text: Connaught Heights Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the floodplain study zones before assuming the west end is clear: the City's study zones the low-lying edges only — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 west-end Fraser River industrial land, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront, Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area — and no zone is named for Connaught Heights' residential streets, which settles the study map, not an individual low lot near Marine Way.

Check the station-area designation before pricing a lot as a house lot: the 22nd Street Station Frequent Transit Development Area in the Official Community Plan directs higher-density growth near the station, so a lot's plan designation and zoning should both be confirmed with the City.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Connaught Heights?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 14 houses listed in Connaught Heights. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Connaught Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Connaught Heights had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Connaught Heights from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses sold in Connaught Heights over those 5 months, out of 75 in all of New Westminster.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Connaught Heights?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain station serves Connaught Heights?
faq.a: 22nd Street Station on the Expo Line is at the neighbourhood, and the Official Community Plan identifies its surroundings as a Frequent Transit Development Area. TransLink routes from the station include the 100 to Marpole, the 101 to Lougheed Station, the 104 to Annacis Island via Queensborough, and the 128 to Braid Station. For a house buyer, the station is the area's defining amenity — and the reason lots near it are planned differently from the interior streets.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Connaught Heights address?
faq.a: For the sample address 2201 London Street — Connaught Heights Elementary itself — the School District No. The locator also shows Montessori (kindergarten to Grade 5) at Connaught Heights Elementary and Early French Immersion at École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary. Catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact house.

faq.q: Can a house here add a suite or a laneway house?
faq.a: Yes, under the same bylaw that zones the lot. The RS districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 allow secondary suites, and laneway and carriage houses are regulated under that bylaw; RS-1 sets a 557.40 square metre (6,000 square foot) minimum site area and a 0.5 floor space ratio, which frames how much floor area a lot can carry. Permitted space should be documented from City permits before it is priced into a purchase.

faq.q: Is Connaught Heights in the floodplain?
faq.a: No floodplain zone for its residential streets is named in the City's floodplain study. The study zones only the city's low-lying edges — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 the west-end Fraser River industrial land, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. That is a study-level answer, not a lot-level one: a specific lot's status is checked with the City, especially on the low ground near Marine Way.

faq.q: What did houses in Connaught Heights sell for?
faq.a: 6 houses sold in Connaught Heights between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,245,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Connaught Heights?
faq.a: The median was 10 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 95.9% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
